title: Phased retirement of compatibility proxy and client-side mapping toolkit
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket coordinates the phased retirement of the compatibility proxy that translates legacy client model aliases, payload encodings, and legacy transport quirks into the unified inference API. The compat proxy was introduced as a stop-gap to avoid breaking older SDKs and OEM integrations, but it now contributes measurable latency, operational complexity, and a class of regressions during rollouts. The goal is to remove the proxy and provide a small client-side mapping toolkit + migration guide that brings customers onto the unified contract with clear fallbacks and observability.
background: Compatibility proxy has been in front of the main routing plane since 2023. Internal telemetry shows 5-8% higher p50 latency for requests hitting the proxy and a recurring class of errors caused by alias-to-model mapping mismatches. Several enterprise customers have requested removal of middleboxes for auditability and to simplify private deployments. We anticipate ~12% of active tokens originate from legacy clients that still depend on legacy aliases or parameter encodings.
scope_changes: In-scope: decommission proxy layer, ship client-side mapping toolkit (JS/Go/Python), update docs and SDKs, add telemetry gating and rollout automation, provide enterprise migration support. Out-of-scope: removal of deprecated server-side model aliases until client adoption reaches gating thresholds; separate sunsetting of legacy auth headers (handled in PM-271839).
migration_plan: Week 0: Public announcement and migration guide published (confluence + in-console banner)
Week 2: Ship client mapping toolkit in JS/Go/Python with automated tests and examples
Week 3-6: Shadow mode — route a mirrored copy through proxy while recording compatibility failures and feature gaps
Week 7: Telemetry gates review; if failures <= 0.5% for 14 days, proceed to gradual cutover
Week 8-12: Gradual traffic cutover by customer cohort (non-enterprise -> enterprise opt-in -> all), with rollback windows and compensation policy
Final cutoff: Hard proxy shutdown target date (tbd based on telemetry and enterprise contracts)
rollout_timeline: 2026-03-22: Client toolkit alpha released to npm/pypi/go proxy
2026-05-03: Decision gate meeting and readiness signoff
2026-06-01: Target hard cutoff for public clients (enterprise exceptions by contract)
acceptance_criteria: Public migration guide with step-by-step upgrade paths published and linked from Console
Client mapping toolkit available in JS/Go/Python with >=90% coverage and E2E examples
Shadow telemetry shows compatibility failures under 0.5% for 14 consecutive days
No regressions in core generation tests (latency and token correctness) across Canary customers
SDK adapters removed from hosted routing once cutover completes and infra tests pass
Enterprise customers with contractual concerns have documented migration plans and rollbacks
rollback_criteria: If compatibility failures exceed 1.5% for a sustained 48-hour window during cutover, or if p95 latency increase >10% for core routes impacting SLA customers, immediately pause cutover, re-enable proxy routing for affected cohorts, and open incident review. Recovery must include a remediation plan and a communication to impacted customers within 24 hours.
notes: 2026-02-24: Eng requested additional telemetry for legacy alias usage counts; added to ENG-72142
2026-03-01: Legal reviewed notification language and required 60-day enterprise notice for some contracts
2026-03-09: Design reviewed migration UX for Console banner and migration flow; minor copy edits requested
2026-03-10: PM signoff to proceed to alpha client kit release
qa_checks: End-to-end generation tests for 30 representative legacy aliases
Load test shadow traffic at 2x current peak to validate routing stability
Backward-compatibility fuzz tests for payload encodings
Automated integration tests for SDK examples and client toolkit
customer_notifications: Targeted emails to customers using legacy aliases with migration steps and support contacts
Workspace-level telemetry export for enterprise admins
postmortem_plan: If any customer-impacting regression occurs during cutover, open a postmortem within 48 hours, include SRE/Engineering/PM/Support, publish a summary in the incident channel, and update migration docs with mitigation steps. Track follow-ups as sub-issues and include timeline and RCA.
implementation_notes: Keep proxy infra available as a fallback toggle for up to 60 days post-cutoff for emergency customer rollbacks. Maintain a compatibility whitelist for customers who cannot migrate within the public timeline; whitelist additions require PM + Legal approval. Coordinate with Dedicated/Private teams to ensure private deployments are not left with invisible routing changes.
